title: queue settings
description: What <app> config queue answers with -o json: how long a change waits for its turn and how long it may hold it, the two settings every app with a change queue has (queue.wait and queue.limit in the app's config.yaml, ADR-S14). Each is at least a second, so a typo never fails every change: the schema refuses zero and units below a second, and mankit's Queue.Settings is the final check.

kind.description: Always QueueSettings, the kind of this answer, so a reader knows which schema its data meets.

data.description: The two settings of the app's change queue.

wait.description: How long a change waits for its turn before it gives up, as the app takes it now.

value.description: The duration in effect, as a Go duration of hours, minutes and seconds such as 45s or 2m0s, never zero or in units below a second: the config's value when it sets one, else the default.

default.description: The duration, in the same form, mankit takes when the config sets none, so a person sees what removing the row would give.

set.description: True when the app's config.yaml sets the row, so a person knows the value is chosen, not the default.

limit.description: How long a change may hold its turn before it is stopped, as the app takes it now.

value.description: The duration in effect, as a Go duration of hours, minutes and seconds such as 45s or 2m0s, never zero or in units below a second: the config's value when it sets one, else the default.

default.description: The duration, in the same form, mankit takes when the config sets none, so a person sees what removing the row would give.

set.description: True when the app's config.yaml sets the row, so a person knows the value is chosen, not the default.
